$comment: Polling the materialize endpoint returns a DELIVERY-STATE document, not a job-status one: no `status`, no `state`, no `progress`, no top-level `jobId`. Completion is derived from `delivered` against the tokens the host asked for. `requested` below is the yardstick every vector is judged against.

vectors.note: everything asked for is on hand and nothing is running — done
the job id lives on activeJob.id, never at the top level; progress is delivered over requested

STOP: `deliveryStateUnknown` means `delivered` is empty for want of an answer, not because the bundle is empty. Never read it as Complete — that is the reading that hands over a bundle the platform could not confirm. Unknown is not terminal, so polling continues.

the remainder can never be produced for this area, so the bundle is as complete as it will ever be. Treating a permanently-absent token as outstanding makes a finished bundle poll its whole budget and then time out. Report the gap; do not wait for it.

STOP: a run reports `completed` even when every token's emit failed — the worker's soft-fail envelope swallows per-token errors. The verdict keys on the TOKENS, not on the word. Believing `completed` is the silent loop where a curator regenerates forever; calling it 'still working' is the ten-minute hang.
the reconciler sweeps a stranded run to `cancelled` rather than `failed`, which kept it out of lastFailed and made a timed-out generation completely silent
the terminal run touched none of what WE asked for — someone else's failed pick is not ours
`available_on_request` and `not_selected` mean nobody has tried yet, which is not a failure and not a permanent gap
STOP: nothing delivered, nothing running, nothing failed is Pending — NEVER Complete. This is the normal state in the seconds after a start, before the job row is visible.
a body that is neither shape still refuses in the platform's own words
